body.statement: Let \(q=1-\alpha\). For every parameter mesh \(\delta\), observation mesh \(h\), and truncation radius \(R\), the primal and dual finite programs defining \(V_{N,h}\), with interval-certified Gaussian cell probabilities and conic curve distances, provide explicit computable lower and upper bounds on \(L_\alpha(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)\). If \(\delta\to0\), \(R\to\infty\), \(hR\to0\), and numerical enclosure errors vanish, the certified gap converges to zero. The resulting envelope rules are asymptotically minimax in the Gaussian shift experiment over all externally randomized measurable interval-section bands; the comparison class is not restricted to bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set.
body.justification: The theorem determines the hard local decision value by converging certified finite programs rather than restating its defining infimum.
body.gap: SchaferStark2009OptimalRegions approximates minimum expected measure using test inversion, and ArmstrongKolesar2018OptimalInference solves scalar convex Gaussian functionals; neither covers nonadditive maximum curve width for unrestricted randomized bands on a piecewise-affine KKT graph.
body.consumer: Researchers receive auditable lower and upper certificates for the unavoidable simultaneous risk-band cost at a chosen predictor and panel configuration.
